title: The Discipline You Don't See
author: Camilo Zambrano
summary: Camilo Zambrano writes an open letter to anyone waking up defeated because they tried and it did not go the way they wanted. He argues that the hustle messaging on social media distorts how we judge ourselves, and that we default to seeing the glass half empty because seeing it half full takes thinking when thinking is hard. Against that, he names the quiet efforts that go unseen, such as showing up tired to play with your kids, staying patient and kind, and simply continuing to try. He widens the meaning of discipline beyond making things happen to include what you do when instincts and emotions take the lead and you must choose between what is easy and what you believe in. The piece closes by urging coherence with your principles and compassion toward yourself as the thing that keeps you grounded. It is a short, personal and encouraging reflection rather than a how-to.
points: Zambrano redefines discipline to include the choice between what is easy and what you believe in when emotions take over, not only the output of routines.
He argues that trying is already progress and that social media shows only snapshots of questionable success, so comparison misleads.
Patience and kindness with your children after a draining day are named as acts of discipline that go unnoticed.
Falling is unavoidable, but getting up and continuing is the choice that counts.
Choosing coherence with your principles and self-compassion keeps a person from losing themselves on the way to the top.
quotes: You might be waking up today defeated because you tried, and it didn’t go like you wanted. You really tried. You are trying every day
The thing is that we like to see the glass half empty because seeing it half full requires thinking, and thinking is hard right now.
What you are not seeing is that you are trying. And trying is already progress, so look, keep trying. And you are figuring things out; it’s just taking time.
What you are not seeing is that you treat your kids with love, you are patient and kind, and that in itself is an act of discipline.
Falling is not optional, but getting up and keeping going is a choice. And you are taking it, every day.

Discipline is not only about making things happen. That matters. But it is also about what you do when your instincts kick in, when emotions take the lead, and when you have to choose between what is easy and what you believe in.
There is no point in reaching the top if you are going to lose yourself in the process. Don’t forget your principles, and in every step, make sure you return.
